summary: Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held an academic post, attested as professor by 1987, at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University.

Vishwanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indology scholar who studied at Elphinstone College from around 1847 to 1851. He served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and as an examiner for the University of Mumbai.

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1943–1947), Joachim Wach (1950), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, and doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1955–1959).
Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist. He completed his MA under Karin Preisendanz (until 2007) and studied under Chlodwig H. Werba and Roque Mesquita.

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Moscow Imperial University (~1896–1900) and the Lazarev Institute (~1900–1903), he held posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973) is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Saint Petersburg State and Moscow State, he lectured at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000) before becoming associate professor (2000) and professor (2006) at the University of Oslo.

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich (1900–1970) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested in 1970 and 1990).
Volkbert Näther is a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg (attested 1975), studying under doctoral supervisor Claus Vogel.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Munich (2006–2012), Lumbini International Research Institute (2012–2015), and University of Bern (attested 2019).

Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kiel, Chiang Mai, and Hamburg, he held posts at Passau, Laos, and Münster, before becoming chair for Thai language and culture at Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz (born 1956) works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1976–1986) and under Anagarika Govinda, he held posts at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and the University of Luxembourg (~2004–2014).
W. F. Jayasuriya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under teachers Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963) and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Regent's Park College, Cheltenham, and Cambridge. He was a Fellow at Christ's College (1888) and later served as headmaster at The Perse School (1902–1928).

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) studied medicine at the University of London and St Bartholomew's Hospital. Working in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held appointments at Cambridge, St John's College, and presided over the Anthropological Society of London (~1921–1922).

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Johns Hopkins. He taught at Johns Hopkins and Government SPM Rajput College before serving as professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1926–1965) and curator at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (1964). He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake was an expert in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was a Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara (attested 1996) and became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula (1907–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated in Peradeniya, Calcutta, and Paris. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964–1969) and held professorial and visiting posts at Northwestern and Oxford.

Walter Bruno Henning (1908–1967) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen (~1926–1930), he held posts at SOAS (~1936–1961), Columbia (~1946–1947), and UC Berkeley (~1961–1967).
